articles.title: Cyber police book 18 for allegedly revealing identity of minor accused in Cheranalloor car crash case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kochi City Cyber police have registered a case against 18 social media handles for allegedly revealing the identity of a 17-year-old accused in the Cheranalloor luxury car crash case. The police registered the case following a directive from the Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Court which had recently taken exception to the continued circulation of social media posts that revealed the teenager’s identity.
The Kochi City Cyber police have registered a case against 18 social media handles for allegedly revealing the identity of a 17-year-old accused in the Cheranalloor luxury car crash case.

The police registered the case following a directive from the Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Court which had recently taken exception to the continued circulation of social media posts that revealed the teenager’s identity.
Online channels and social media influencers are among those booked, according to the police.

The case has been registered against Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, which strictly prohibits the disclosure of a child’s identity in any media or public communication, according to the police. The charge, if proven, can attract imprisonment up to six months and a fine up to ₹2 lakh. “Section 351 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) which deals with the offence of criminal intimidation has also been invoked considering the nature of some of the social media posts,” a police officer said.

The court had recently directed the cyber police to take down every social media account and post that is revealing the identity of the child in conflict with law. The court proceeded to order the police to submit a report on the action taken against such posts.

The accused teenager has been booked for allegedly causing the accident in which Jayabalakrishnan, a 55-year-old wayside eatery owner, was killed near Cheranalloor in the early hours of October 25. Jayabalakrishnan was killed after the luxury car, allegedly driven by the minor, rammed the scooter he was riding.

articles.title: Ajit Doval meets Vietnam President To Lam, briefs him on visit outcomes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: National Security Adviser (NSA) Ajit Doval has met Vietnam's President To Lam during his visit to Hanoi and briefed him on the outcomes of his discussions with the Southeast Asian country's senior leaders.
Mr. Doval, who visited Vietnam on November 1-2, called on Mr. Lam, who is also the General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam, and conveyed the greetings of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Mr. Doval thanked Mr. Lam "for his steadfast support in strengthening the India-Vietnam Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," the Indian Embassy in Hanoi said in a post on X on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

During the meeting, Mr. Doval briefed the President on the outcomes of his discussions with Vietnamese leaders and recalled the Vietnamese President's State visit to India in May, according to the embassy.

The National Security Advisor also met Vietnam's Minister of Public Security General Luong Tam Quang, and the two sides discussed cooperation in law enforcement, cyber, maritime and economic security, the embassy said.
They agreed to strengthen capacity building in these areas, it said.
The embassy said the discussions reflected the "deep and mutually trusted civilisational partnership between India and Vietnam".
India, Vietnam deepen defence cooperation with focus on maritime security
The two sides also exchanged views on regional and global developments.

Mr. Doval also met Vietnam's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence, General Phan Van Giang, to review ongoing bilateral defence cooperation and agree to strengthen engagement in the sector further.

He also met Foreign Affairs Minister Le Hoai Trung, with the two sides discussing ways to commemorate the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between India and Vietnam in 2027.
The embassy said the anniversary would be marked in the spirit of the Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: No loss of life in Andhra Pradesh due to Cyclone Murasu, says NDRF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: In an effort to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu, the Andhra Pradesh government’s Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) has rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism through its ‘Mana Mitra’ WhatsApp Governance platform, an official release said on Monday.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.

The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.

According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. - ANI
Hand-in-hand with emergency crews, our army of government officials is facing the full brunt of #CycloneMurasu to keep Andhra Pradesh safe.
No casualties have been recorded in Andhra Pradesh till now due to Cyclone Murasu, the NDRF said.

The federal contingency force has deployed 14 teams in the coastal State that has been the “most affected” by the cyclone, Mohsen Shahedi, DIG, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), told reporters at a press briefing.

Severe cyclonic storm Murasu has made landfall near Ongole, South Andhra Pradesh bringing torrential rain and gale-force winds up to 100 kmph across the region. The severe weather system has severely disrupted normal life in Prakasam district and surrounding areas.

To ensure passenger safety and safe train operations, the Vijayawada Division of South Coast Railway has suspended train movements on the Vijayawada-Ongole-Gudur section until further notice. Passengers planning to travel through these routes are stritly advised to verify running status on official channels such as NTES app. -- The Hindu Bureau

Three districts in Telangana were placed under red alert — indicating possibility of extremely heavy rain — on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), under the impact of the severe cyclonic storm Murasu (war drum). The eye of the storm crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast at 5.30 a.m.

While Nalgonda and Nagakurnool were earlier placed under the weather alert, India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre on Tuesday has forecast extremely heavy rain in Suryapet, Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts. -- The Hindu Bureau

Naguluppalapadu mandal in Prakasam district recorded the highest rainfall of 198 mm in the 24 hours ending at 8.30 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), as Cyclone Murasu brought heavy to very heavy rainfall across several parts of the district. Kothapatnam mandal followed with 182.3 mm, while Ongole Urban recorded 174.7 mm during the same period. The cyclone hit near Kothapatnam beach on the shore of Bay of Bengal.

articles.title: Poultry industry pushes for ₹110 per kg live chicken price
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Concerned over recent fluctuations in broiler chicken prices and rising input costs, poultry industry leaders from across the country have called for coordinated efforts to stabilise the market and maintain a benchmark price of ₹110 per kg for live chicken.

The decision was taken at a high-level meeting held in Hyderabad on Monday (November 2, 2026), where representatives of the All India Poultry Breeders Association (AIPBA), Pan India Breeders Coordination Committee (PIBCC) and several State poultry associations discussed the challenges confronting the poultry sector.

Industry leaders observed that the recent decline in chicken prices was largely seasonal, coinciding with reduced consumption during the festival period, and urged stakeholders not to panic. They resolved to meet government representatives and policymakers in New Delhi next week to discuss these issues and other pressing challenges facing the poultry industry.

The leaders emphasised the need for policy interventions to address rising feed costs, particularly by facilitating duty-free imports of non-genetically modified (non-GMO) maize. Highlighting the abundant availability of soybean in the market, the participants urged poultry farmers and other stakeholders not to panic over the recent price fluctuations, which they described as temporary.

The challenges posed by rising maize prices amid shortages in availability attributed to the impact of El Niño conditions and their impact on poultry production costs were discussed at the meeting. Industry representatives stressed the need for collective efforts to ensure price stability and protect the interests of poultry farmers and other stakeholders.
AIPBA chairman Bahadur Ali, PIBCC convenor Vasanth Kumar Shetty, Telangana Poultry Breeders Association (TPBA) president A. Tirupathi Reddy and other industry representatives attended the meeting.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: floodwater recedes, but damaged roads remain a concern in Chennai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: As cyclone Murasu brought overnight rains lashing the city from Sunday (November 1, 2026) night, rainwater stagnation reported in several parts of Chennai had receded by 11 a.m. on Monday (November 2). However, damaged roads, potholes and stretches left uneven after stormwater drain and utility works continued to trouble residents and councillors of Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC). they urged the civic body to rectify problems before next rains due to Northeast monsoon hit the city in December.

According to Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) of GCC, Chennai recorded an average rainfall of 76.07 mm in the 24 hours ending at 6 a.m. on November 2, according to data from the Greater Chennai Corporation’s Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC). Of the monitoring stations, 28 recorded heavy rain and five recorded very heavy rain. Parrys recorded the highest rainfall at 149.2 mm, followed by New Manali Town at 141.6 mm.

Rainfall intensity eased considerably on November 2. The city recorded an average of 2.08 mm between 6 a.m. and 2 p.m. During this eight-hour period, 47 stations recorded very light rain and 16 recorded light rain. Ennore recorded the highest rainfall at 5.6 mm.

Ambedkar Valavan aka Kumarasamy, VCK party councillor of Purasaiwalkam, said there was no water stagnation in his ward, including Thideer Nagar and Periyar Nagar. He said earlier works had addressed the waterlogging problems reported in the area. However, he flagged the poor condition of several roads, including Rettamalai Srinivasan Salai and Cooks Road, from Otteri Bridge towards Binny Mills, where potholes and uneven surfaces remained.

Following the rains from Cyclone Murasu, stagnant rainwater was being drained at Sai Nagar 9th Cross Street in Thoraipakkam under Sholinganallur Zone by Greater Chennai Corporation on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

He said several roads in Thiru.Vi.Ka Nagar Zone, including New Barren Road, Kunnur High Road, Strahans Road, Perambur Barracks Road, Ganeshapuram Road, Ambedkar College Road and Basin Bridge Road, had been affected by excavation works for Metro Rail and Metro Water projects. Sections had been dug up and left uneven without proper restoration, he said. Even light rain could make such stretches hazardous for motorists, particularly those unfamiliar with the road conditions.

He also flagged the continued closure of the Ganeshapuram subway despite the road work not progressing. The closure had forced residents of surrounding neighbourhoods to take longer routes to reach cremation grounds. Residents who could earlier reach the B.B. Road crematorium after travelling about half a kilometre now had to travel nearly eight km, he said.

Following the rains from Cyclone Murasu, repair work is underway to fix potholes formed on the road at Ponniamman Koil Street near Manjambakkam under Manali Zone by the Greater Chennai Corporation on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Mr. Kumarasamy alleged that road works awarded during the previous regime had been stopped after the change of government, with officials citing a lack of funds. He said estimates and repair works had not been prepared in advance of the monsoon. He also criticised the absence of advance arrangements such as deploying tractors, generators and pumps in vulnerable locations.

K. Shanmugam, president of the Federation of North Chennai Resident Welfare Associations, said the rain had not caused major flooding in his area. However, water collected in depressions along the road from Chinnamadam to Thiruthangal Nadar College because of its uneven surface. He also flagged K.K. Salai in Manali, a key link road stretching about two–three km towards Manali market, where sections had been dug up for stormwater drain works but had not been properly restored.
Greater Chennai corporation attening to potholes in Kumaran Nagar in Madhavaram on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

S. Vishanth of the Ennore Solidarity Group said water had stagnated in parts of Athipattu near Ennore, but the situation had subsequently improved. He said the area where he was located was relatively elevated and had experienced less water accumulation.

articles.title: What is ‘Guidance’, Tamil Nadu’s nodal agency for investments? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The story so far: Guidance, the nodal agency of the Tamil Nadu government for investment promotion and single-window facilitation, is in the limelight for the wrong reasons. Former Chief Ministers M.K. Stalin and Edappadi K. Palaniswami have accused the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government of having “immobilised” the body.

Guidance, earlier known as the Tamil Nadu Guidance and Export Promotion Bureau, was established as a non-profit registered society on July 15, 1992, with the objective of attracting investment proposals into Tamil Nadu. It is mandated to span the full spectrum of investment promotion activities, with a focus on generating leads, facilitating projects, and providing post-investment support. The body is expected to catch the emerging market trends and formulate new sectoral policies, strengthen industry-academia collaboration, and engage with trade bodies and multilateral agencies. It hopes to play a crucial role in making the State a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036, a goal of the present government.

articles.title: Petronet LNG reports 52.3% growth in net profits, in talks for availing undelivered cargoes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia.
The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share.
The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year.
Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore.
The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year.
Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year.
Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year.

Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure.
“On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said.
The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end.
Mr. Singh told reporters that the contractual terms have provisions to recoup the lost cargoes for one year after the expiry of the current contract period, that is, May 2028.
He stated that Petronet LNG lost an average 9-10 cargoes each month in the last eight months, thus, about 75-80 cargoes whilst it has received 6 cargoes from the supplier.

articles.title: Congress seeks JPC probe into IDBI Bank sale, alleges valuation irregularities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Congress on Monday (November 2, 2026) demanded an immediate halt to the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings and a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) probe into the transaction, alleging that the government had manipulated the bank’s valuation.
The party alleged that the foreign buyer would use the bank’s own funds to finance the acquisition.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh separately described the transaction as a “major scam” by the Narendra Modi government and demanded that both valuation reports be made public.
Addressing a press conference, senior Congress leader Shaktisinh Gohil alleged that the disinvestment process was riddled with irregularities and lacked transparency.

Citing a conversation between an analyst and Fairfax Chairman Prem Watsa and President Peter Clarke, Mr. Gohil claimed that the company had indicated that the payment would be made in instalments, with the initial investment followed by the use of IDBI Bank’s resources to meet the remaining acquisition cost.
“Prem Watsa is a very close to Modi ji and had showered praise on him during the 2017 Vibrant Gujarat Summit,” the Congress leader said.

Mr. Gohil questioned the rationale of selling a profitable Indian bank to a foreign company using its own funds. He said IDBI Bank had earned a cumulative profit of ₹30,105 crore between 2021 and 2026 and had non-performing assets of only about 2%.
Its profit per employee stood at ₹49.8 lakh, making it one of the leading banks on this measure, he said. “Why is a bank that is delivering such high profits being sold?” he asked.

The Congress leader also questioned the revision of the bank’s valuation from ₹94.42 to ₹75 a share after the bids had been opened. He said the government had initially fixed the valuation at ₹94.42 a share before inviting bids, but subsequently revised it downwards.
The government was now claiming to have secured a good deal by selling the bank at ₹81 a share, he said, demanding disclosure of both valuation reports and the identity of the second bidder.

Mr. Gohil invoked an assurance given by the then Finance Minister Jaswant Singh in Parliament in August 2003 that the government’s stake in IDBI Bank would not be reduced below 51%. A Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance had also favoured retaining the government’s majority stake, he said.

He further questioned the regulatory concessions extended to Fairfax, including the two-year window reportedly allowed to reduce its control in another Indian bank, and sought details of the source of funds for the acquisition.

articles.title: Capex push to continue, but fiscal prudence non-negotiable: FM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to sustaining capital expenditure (capex) to support economic growth, while stressing that fiscal prudence would remain non-negotiable.

“Capex is a very important component of our growth strategy. Because till such time the private sector will be able to expand capacity or make capital investment, it is important for the Government to push through with capital investment,” she said at an event organised by HSBC India in Mumbai.
Pointing to the returns from public investment over the past four to five years, she said the multiplier effects had strengthened the Government’s confidence in continuing the spending push.

“We find that in the last 4 to 5 years, we have got very good success. The multipliers actually work and it gives us confidence that the Government is not going to sit back and watch whether growth is growing without doing much,” she said.

The Government would be willing to extend capex support to ensure that the growth momentum was not disrupted. “We will continue doing that because India’s growth momentum should not be lost at all,” she said.
However, Ms. Sitharaman made it clear that higher public spending would have to be balanced against fiscal constraints.
“We need to be fiscally prudent,” she said, adding that while some advocated spending without worrying about sovereign credit ratings, responsible expenditure was essential.
“I agree we need to spend but it has to be done responsibly and fiscal prudence will be our top priority,” she emphasised.
“We have to be prudent and we have to be creative based on which we can encourage growth and stability,” she added.
The Finance Minister also called for greater confidence in India’s economic prospects, urging businesses and experts to move beyond pessimism and sector-specific concerns.

“India must to talk with optimism and there needs to be reduction in cynicism,” she said, questioning why experts who considered their own sectors healthy remained apprehensive about the broader economy.
“If your sector doing fine, others sectors in India must be similarly fine. So can the narrate and language change?” she asked.

articles.title: No-cost EMI: a loan that is portrayed as free

fullParagraphs: Every festive season, the same board greets you at the electronics shop: “No-cost EMI”. TVs, washing machines and appliances are available at no-cost EMI. A ₹60,000 phone, 6 easy instalments of ₹10,000, no interest. It feels as if the shopkeeper has done you a favour. He has not. Nobody lends money for free and nobody sells at a loss. Someone pays. Lets see who.

A bank or finance firm funds the purchase and charges interest. The shop agrees to bear interest but it will recover it in one of two ways. Either the price quoted to you is higher, or you lose the discount a cash buyer would have got Take the same phone. A cash buyer gets it for ₹57,000. The EMI buyer pays ₹60,000. The ₹3,000 gap is the interest.

About evacuation, it said that it loaded on an average 310 rakes per day — to the power sector — in October.

articles.title: Child dies of measles in New York's first such death in 30 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A child in rural northern New York has died after contracting measles, marking the State's first death from the disease in 30 years, state officials announced on Monday (November 2, 2026).
The child died in Lewis County, about 93 miles (150 kilometres) north of Syracuse, Governor Kathy Hochul said.

The U.S. stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease.

Ms. Hochul, a Democrat, said the child's death is “a devastating reminder of what's at stake when Washington deliberately erodes decades of progress in protecting Americans from preventable illnesses.”

The Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed three measles-associated deaths in the U.S. this year, but State health departments have reported higher numbers. Pennsylvania health officials have reported five deaths this year and are investigating a possible sixth.

Ms. Hochul declared a disaster emergency in early October because of measles cases in neighbouring States and in rural areas of New York. The executive order extended the pool of people who can administer measles vaccines to include paramedics, midwives and others, and it allowed nurses to join doctors in ordering testing.

fullParagraphs: The story so far: Early morning on October 29, many customers at Binance, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world, began receiving messages that their accounts were being unexpectedly emptied. What followed, over the course of just about 20 minutes, was the biggest crypto hack in history, with more than $6 billion worth being stolen. By November 2, Binance had replaced 100% of the stolen amount to customers. The search for the culprit and recovery process still continues, but the customer impact has been mitigated in a remarkably short time.

Cryptocurrency transactions involve a multi-rung authentication involving public keys as well as private keys that are held by each user. According to Binance, a preliminary investigation points to a “compromised” laptop belonging to one of its engineers that could have allowed the hacker to submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.

articles.title: California could become the first State to tax billionaires' wealth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: California could become the first State in the nation to tax the net worth of billionaires , it was proposed on Tuesday (November 3. 2026) under a ballot measure that has divided liberal leaders nationally and triggered one of the most expensive ballot fights in the State’s history as the ultra-rich scramble to figure out whether they would pay the tax or flee.
Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion, with most of the revenue dedicated to replacing federal funding cuts to healthcare.

Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders has framed the proposal as a monumental step toward reining in deep wealth inequality by ensuring the ultra-rich pay their fair share. But Democratic Governor Gavin Newsom warns it would prompt the State's wealthiest to move out of California and take their tax money with them.

The “no” side has raised roughly 10 times as much as the “yes” side, thanks in large part to tech moguls and venture capitalists, who have poured millions into a political action committee fighting the measure. Billionaires are already bracing for its approval. Some of them, including Google co-founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page, started cutting ties with the State after the measure was unveiled. Mark Zuckerberg said he would stay in California for eight years and made a deal with Meta that would help him pay the tax without losing his ownership stake in the company.

Backers of the proposed tax, led by the powerful labor union SEIU United Healthcare Workers West, say it's needed to help the State backfill the federal funding cuts. The union estimates the state will lose $100 billion in federal healthcare funding over five years.
“It's time to collect those taxes so we can ensure that our healthcare system is still safe,” said Lorena Gonzalez, president of the California Federation of Labor Unions.

But some traditional Democratic allies, including Planned Parenthood and the California Teachers Association, are part of a coalition opposing it. They're concerned about how the tax revenue would be divvied up and about the potential impact on the State's budget if there's a mass exodus of wealthy taxpayers. California's budget relies heavily on the income tax of the State's richest residents.

Likely voters were slightly more likely to oppose the measure than support it in a poll conducted in mid-October by the Public Policy Institute of California, with 52% saying they would vote “no” and 46% saying they would vote “yes.” That's an apparent shift from a PPIC survey conducted in early September, when 52% of likely voters said they'd vote for the tax and 46% said they'd vote against it.
Robert Swonger, an auto glass technician living near Sacramento who's politically independent, said he planned to vote against it.
“Obviously, I would like billionaires not to have as much money as they do,” he said. “But I don't believe taxing them out of existence is going to work.”

Anthony Serrano, a Democrat living in Folsom who works for Kaiser Permanente, one of the nation's largest not-for-profit healthcare plans, said he was leaning toward voting for the tax because he tends to support “anything that is a positive for healthcare.”

Even if the measure wins approval from a majority of voters, it would be blocked from taking effect if at least one of two measures designed to nullify it, which are also on this year's ballot, passes and receives more “yes” votes. The proposals, which are backed by the political action committee Building a Better California, include a ban on new taxes on financial assets and other personal property, a category that excludes real estate. The committee has raised more than $333 million, about 30% of it from Brin.

articles.title: India, Israel vote against UNGA draft on regional conventional arms control
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: India and Israel have voted against a draft resolution in the United Nations by Pakistan and Belarus on conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels, with New Delhi saying countries' security concerns are not confined within regional boundaries.

The draft resolution, titled ‘General and complete disarmament: Conventional arms control at the regional and subregional levels’, was approved by the UN General Assembly’s First Committee on Monday (November 2, 2026) with 180 votes in favour, two against and no abstentions.
India and Israel were the only countries to vote against the resolution in the 193-member UN body.
Explaining India's vote, First Secretary at India’s Permanent Mission to the UN, Anmol Sher Bedi said conventional arms control was a global issue.
“We are not fully convinced that it should be pursued primarily in regional and sub-regional contexts,” Bedi said while delivering India’s Explanation of Vote in the UNGA First Committee.
He said New Delhi voted against the resolution consistent with its past position.

India also questioned the resolution's request to the UN Disarmament Commission to consider formulating principles that could serve as a framework for regional agreements on conventional arms control.
“We read this request with a certain degree of curiosity,” Bedi said.

He pointed out that the Commission had already adopted by consensus guidelines and recommendations on regional disarmament in 1993, guidelines on conventional arms control and disarmament in 1999, and recommendations on practical confidence-building measures in the field of conventional weapons in 2017.
“That makes three consensus outcomes on this very subject in the very body now being asked to start from scratch,” he said.
“We fail to understand why a subject already deliberated at length needs another round of deliberation unless the aim is to keep the UN disarmament machinery busy,” Bedi added.
Bedi also objected to the resolution's approach towards maintaining a balance in defence capabilities within a region or subregion.

articles.title: Who are the Indian-origin candidates in U.S. midterm elections?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Indian-origin candidates are seeking office across the United States in the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, the polls are so called because they fall midway through a President’s four-year term

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are due for election, since members serve two-year terms. In the Senate, where members serve six years, 35 of the 100 seats are up for election, including special elections in Ohio and Florida.

The Indian-origin candidates are contesting from States including California, Washington, Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Ohio, New York and Maryland. Their races span different levels of government, from the U.S. Congress and State executive offices to city leadership positions.

Several Indian-Americans are in the fray across Texas, Florida, Arizona, Ohio, New York and Los Angeles. Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress.
Here are some of the prominent Indian-origin candidates contesting the midterm elections:

Congressman Ro Khanna is a member of the progressive wing of the Democratic Party. His grandfather, Amarnath Vidyalankar, was a freedom fighter who was imprisoned alongside Mahatma Gandhi and later served as a Congress Member of Parliament.

Mr. Khanna is a second-generation immigrant. His father, a chemical engineer from the Indian Institute of Technology, and his mother, a school teacher, migrated to the United States from Punjab. Born in Philadelphia, Mr. Khanna studied economics at the University of Chicago before earning a law degree from Yale Law School. He later worked as an intellectual property lawyer with clients from the technology sector.

A Democrat from California, Mr. Khanna is seeking re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, which includes parts of Silicon Valley. articles.title: Child dies of measles in New York's first such death in 30 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: A child in rural northern New York has died after contracting measles, marking the State's first death from the disease in 30 years, state officials announced on Monday (November 2, 2026).
The child died in Lewis County, about 93 miles (150 kilometres) north of Syracuse, Governor Kathy Hochul said.

The U.S. stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease.

Ms. Hochul, a Democrat, said the child's death is “a devastating reminder of what's at stake when Washington deliberately erodes decades of progress in protecting Americans from preventable illnesses.”

The Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed three measles-associated deaths in the U.S. this year, but State health departments have reported higher numbers. Pennsylvania health officials have reported five deaths this year and are investigating a possible sixth.

Ms. Hochul declared a disaster emergency in early October because of measles cases in neighbouring States and in rural areas of New York. The executive order extended the pool of people who can administer measles vaccines to include paramedics, midwives and others, and it allowed nurses to join doctors in ordering testing.

articles.title: Binance’s recovery from the biggest crypto hack in history | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The story so far: Early morning on October 29, many customers at Binance, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world, began receiving messages that their accounts were being unexpectedly emptied. What followed, over the course of just about 20 minutes, was the biggest crypto hack in history, with more than $6 billion worth being stolen. By November 2, Binance had replaced 100% of the stolen amount to customers. The search for the culprit and recovery process still continues, but the customer impact has been mitigated in a remarkably short time.

Cryptocurrency transactions involve a multi-rung authentication involving public keys as well as private keys that are held by each user. According to Binance, a preliminary investigation points to a “compromised” laptop belonging to one of its engineers that could have allowed the hacker to submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.

articles.title: Initiative to strengthen perinatal mental healthcare to be piloted in T.N.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu is preparing to pilot an initiative to strengthen perinatal mental healthcare by making screening available at the primary healthcare level. As a part of the initiative, Village Health Nurses (VHNs) and medical officers are being trained to screen pregnant women for mental health problems, particularly depression, during the antenatal and postnatal periods and facilitate timely and appropriate care.

The ‘Thai Manam’ project is set to be piloted, with VHNs and medical officers in four blocks of Villupuram district — Kanai, Koliyanur, Vallam, and Mugaiyur — who are undergoing training as part of a collaborative initiative involving the Institute of Mental Health (IMH), Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Epidemiology, and the Directorate of Public Health (DPH) and Preventive Medicine.

articles.title: Apple posts stronger-than-expected Q4 revenue in first earnings report for new CEO John Ternus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Apple Inc. posted stronger-than-expected revenue in the fiscal fourth quarter, giving new CEO John Ternus an upbeat start to his tenure, which began in September. The solid results bucked a downward trend for tech giants this quarter, as companies including Alphabet, Amazon and Intel had disappointing quarterly results.

The Cupertino, California-based company earned $30.71 billion, or $2.10 per share, in the July-September period. That's up 12% from $27.47 billion, or $1.85 per share, in the same period a year earlier. Apple said its earnings included 5 cents per share from tariff refunds.
Revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion from $102.5 billion.
Analysts, on average, were expecting earnings of $1.99 per share on revenue of $113.4 billion, according to a poll by FactSet.

“Apple’s strong earnings come in the wake of a recent tech sell-off, as investors question the enormous cost and uncertain returns of the AI boom driven by Apple’s Big Tech counterparts," said Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne, adding that record iPhone revenue and strong growth in China demonstrate the resilience of Apple's business.

While its rivals are facing investor uncertainty over massive investments in artificial intelligence, Bourne said Apple's “tepid approach" to AI infrastructure spending helps preserve its cash flow — while partnerships with companies like Alphabet could help Apple to strengthen its AI capabilities without taking on the same financial risks as its peers.

Despite the solid quarterly numbers, Apple said its closely watched gross margin, which was 47.9% during the fourth quarter, will be lower in the December quarter — between 45% and 46% — primarily due to higher memory costs and expenses related to its release of Siri AI.
While Apple's stock was flat after the earnings numbers came out, it declined 2.6% to $329.60 during the earnings call. The stock had closed down 1.8% at $338.32 in regular trading.

articles.title: Anthropic says revenue surged 1100% ahead of IPO

fullParagraphs: Anthropic, one of the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, on Monday reported a more than 1,100 percent surge in quarterly revenue as it counts down to going public on Wall Street later this month.
Anthropic's listing, expected as early as next week, comes amid growing nervousness among investors about the huge sums being poured into AI.
Revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier.

The company, whose stock market debut will help determine how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last, said in an amended filing that its net loss reached $23.3 billion in the July-September period.
The loss stemmed mostly from non-cash accounting charges linked to the company's rising valuation, the filing showed.
The filing also showed Anthropic has committed to spend about $895 billion, mostly on computing power, much of it over the next five years.
It slipped back to an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter as it paid more for short-term computing capacity.

The IPO will be a major test of the market's faith in the AI boom, with the pool of potential investors set to widen as retail traders get their first chance to buy shares directly in a standalone AI giant.
Last week, skittishness about AI spending triggered a sharp sell-off in big tech stocks after the latest earnings showed massive investment without clear enough signs of a return.

Anthropic's roughly 400-page filing devotes more than 90 pages to risks, including those facing an industry that has seen a string of reports in recent months of AI systems behaving in unexpected and harmful ways.

articles.title: United stand: On protests against SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.

The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. The call for the restoration of institutional integrity is the need of the hour; but Mr. Gandhi must be careful not to misstate the nature of the crisis. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.

articles.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.
• The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

articles.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 28, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited for standing firm on the issue , opposing the embargo, and calling for “dialogue and diplomacy” in its statement. The vote came a month after the BRICS New Delhi declaration expressed “deep concern” over the tightening of unilateral blockade measures on Cuba, and the “worrying humanitarian impact” on the Cuban people. It is important that India continue to stand up to such unilateral measures and amplify the voice of smaller countries, particularly those in the Global South.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.

articles.title: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. The Union Government claims that the country’s social security coverage has increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025, which is around 94 crore citizens. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. Almost two decades ago, the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, headed by economist Arjun Sengupta, recommended a slew of measures to improve the social security of workers in the informal sector. The issues raised by the panel still remain unaddressed. A report prepared by Justice V. Gopala Gowda for the Keralam Government in March this year flagged certain anti-federal and anti-worker characteristics in the Social Security Code and suggested amendments. The Union Government should take the trade unions and the State Governments on board while creating new systems and mechanisms to address the social security concerns of the vast majority of workers.

articles.title: Cyber police book 18 for allegedly revealing identity of minor accused in Cheranalloor car crash case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kochi City Cyber police have registered a case against 18 social media handles for allegedly revealing the identity of a 17-year-old accused in the Cheranalloor luxury car crash case. The police registered the case following a directive from the Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Court which had recently taken exception to the continued circulation of social media posts that revealed the teenager’s identity.
The Kochi City Cyber police have registered a case against 18 social media handles for allegedly revealing the identity of a 17-year-old accused in the Cheranalloor luxury car crash case.

The police registered the case following a directive from the Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Court which had recently taken exception to the continued circulation of social media posts that revealed the teenager’s identity.
Online channels and social media influencers are among those booked, according to the police.

The case has been registered against Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, which strictly prohibits the disclosure of a child’s identity in any media or public communication, according to the police. The charge, if proven, can attract imprisonment up to six months and a fine up to ₹2 lakh. “Section 351 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) which deals with the offence of criminal intimidation has also been invoked considering the nature of some of the social media posts,” a police officer said.

The court had recently directed the cyber police to take down every social media account and post that is revealing the identity of the child in conflict with law. The court proceeded to order the police to submit a report on the action taken against such posts.

The accused teenager has been booked for allegedly causing the accident in which Jayabalakrishnan, a 55-year-old wayside eatery owner, was killed near Cheranalloor in the early hours of October 25. Jayabalakrishnan was killed after the luxury car, allegedly driven by the minor, rammed the scooter he was riding.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: National Security Adviser (NSA) Ajit Doval has met Vietnam's President To Lam during his visit to Hanoi and briefed him on the outcomes of his discussions with the Southeast Asian country's senior leaders.
Mr. Doval, who visited Vietnam on November 1-2, called on Mr. Lam, who is also the General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam, and conveyed the greetings of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Mr. Doval thanked Mr. Lam "for his steadfast support in strengthening the India-Vietnam Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," the Indian Embassy in Hanoi said in a post on X on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

During the meeting, Mr. Doval briefed the President on the outcomes of his discussions with Vietnamese leaders and recalled the Vietnamese President's State visit to India in May, according to the embassy.

The National Security Advisor also met Vietnam's Minister of Public Security General Luong Tam Quang, and the two sides discussed cooperation in law enforcement, cyber, maritime and economic security, the embassy said.
They agreed to strengthen capacity building in these areas, it said.
The embassy said the discussions reflected the "deep and mutually trusted civilisational partnership between India and Vietnam".
India, Vietnam deepen defence cooperation with focus on maritime security
The two sides also exchanged views on regional and global developments.

Mr. Doval also met Vietnam's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence, General Phan Van Giang, to review ongoing bilateral defence cooperation and agree to strengthen engagement in the sector further.

He also met Foreign Affairs Minister Le Hoai Trung, with the two sides discussing ways to commemorate the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between India and Vietnam in 2027.
The embassy said the anniversary would be marked in the spirit of the Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: No loss of life in Andhra Pradesh due to Cyclone Murasu, says NDRF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: In an effort to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu, the Andhra Pradesh government’s Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) has rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism through its ‘Mana Mitra’ WhatsApp Governance platform, an official release said on Monday.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.

The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.

According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. - ANI
Hand-in-hand with emergency crews, our army of government officials is facing the full brunt of #CycloneMurasu to keep Andhra Pradesh safe.
No casualties have been recorded in Andhra Pradesh till now due to Cyclone Murasu, the NDRF said.

The federal contingency force has deployed 14 teams in the coastal State that has been the “most affected” by the cyclone, Mohsen Shahedi, DIG, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), told reporters at a press briefing.

Severe cyclonic storm Murasu has made landfall near Ongole, South Andhra Pradesh bringing torrential rain and gale-force winds up to 100 kmph across the region. The severe weather system has severely disrupted normal life in Prakasam district and surrounding areas.

To ensure passenger safety and safe train operations, the Vijayawada Division of South Coast Railway has suspended train movements on the Vijayawada-Ongole-Gudur section until further notice. Passengers planning to travel through these routes are stritly advised to verify running status on official channels such as NTES app. -- The Hindu Bureau

Three districts in Telangana were placed under red alert — indicating possibility of extremely heavy rain — on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), under the impact of the severe cyclonic storm Murasu (war drum). The eye of the storm crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast at 5.30 a.m.

While Nalgonda and Nagakurnool were earlier placed under the weather alert, India Meteorological Department-Hyderabad Centre on Tuesday has forecast extremely heavy rain in Suryapet, Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts. -- The Hindu Bureau

Naguluppalapadu mandal in Prakasam district recorded the highest rainfall of 198 mm in the 24 hours ending at 8.30 a.m. on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), as Cyclone Murasu brought heavy to very heavy rainfall across several parts of the district. Kothapatnam mandal followed with 182.3 mm, while Ongole Urban recorded 174.7 mm during the same period. The cyclone hit near Kothapatnam beach on the shore of Bay of Bengal.

articles.title: Poultry industry pushes for ₹110 per kg live chicken price
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Concerned over recent fluctuations in broiler chicken prices and rising input costs, poultry industry leaders from across the country have called for coordinated efforts to stabilise the market and maintain a benchmark price of ₹110 per kg for live chicken.

The decision was taken at a high-level meeting held in Hyderabad on Monday (November 2, 2026), where representatives of the All India Poultry Breeders Association (AIPBA), Pan India Breeders Coordination Committee (PIBCC) and several State poultry associations discussed the challenges confronting the poultry sector.

Industry leaders observed that the recent decline in chicken prices was largely seasonal, coinciding with reduced consumption during the festival period, and urged stakeholders not to panic. They resolved to meet government representatives and policymakers in New Delhi next week to discuss these issues and other pressing challenges facing the poultry industry.

The leaders emphasised the need for policy interventions to address rising feed costs, particularly by facilitating duty-free imports of non-genetically modified (non-GMO) maize. Highlighting the abundant availability of soybean in the market, the participants urged poultry farmers and other stakeholders not to panic over the recent price fluctuations, which they described as temporary.

The challenges posed by rising maize prices amid shortages in availability attributed to the impact of El Niño conditions and their impact on poultry production costs were discussed at the meeting. Industry representatives stressed the need for collective efforts to ensure price stability and protect the interests of poultry farmers and other stakeholders.
AIPBA chairman Bahadur Ali, PIBCC convenor Vasanth Kumar Shetty, Telangana Poultry Breeders Association (TPBA) president A. Tirupathi Reddy and other industry representatives attended the meeting.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: floodwater recedes, but damaged roads remain a concern in Chennai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: As cyclone Murasu brought overnight rains lashing the city from Sunday (November 1, 2026) night, rainwater stagnation reported in several parts of Chennai had receded by 11 a.m. on Monday (November 2). However, damaged roads, potholes and stretches left uneven after stormwater drain and utility works continued to trouble residents and councillors of Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC). they urged the civic body to rectify problems before next rains due to Northeast monsoon hit the city in December.

According to Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) of GCC, Chennai recorded an average rainfall of 76.07 mm in the 24 hours ending at 6 a.m. on November 2, according to data from the Greater Chennai Corporation’s Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC). Of the monitoring stations, 28 recorded heavy rain and five recorded very heavy rain. Parrys recorded the highest rainfall at 149.2 mm, followed by New Manali Town at 141.6 mm.

Rainfall intensity eased considerably on November 2. The city recorded an average of 2.08 mm between 6 a.m. and 2 p.m. During this eight-hour period, 47 stations recorded very light rain and 16 recorded light rain. Ennore recorded the highest rainfall at 5.6 mm.

Ambedkar Valavan aka Kumarasamy, VCK party councillor of Purasaiwalkam, said there was no water stagnation in his ward, including Thideer Nagar and Periyar Nagar. He said earlier works had addressed the waterlogging problems reported in the area. However, he flagged the poor condition of several roads, including Rettamalai Srinivasan Salai and Cooks Road, from Otteri Bridge towards Binny Mills, where potholes and uneven surfaces remained.

Following the rains from Cyclone Murasu, stagnant rainwater was being drained at Sai Nagar 9th Cross Street in Thoraipakkam under Sholinganallur Zone by Greater Chennai Corporation on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

He said several roads in Thiru.Vi.Ka Nagar Zone, including New Barren Road, Kunnur High Road, Strahans Road, Perambur Barracks Road, Ganeshapuram Road, Ambedkar College Road and Basin Bridge Road, had been affected by excavation works for Metro Rail and Metro Water projects. Sections had been dug up and left uneven without proper restoration, he said. Even light rain could make such stretches hazardous for motorists, particularly those unfamiliar with the road conditions.

He also flagged the continued closure of the Ganeshapuram subway despite the road work not progressing. The closure had forced residents of surrounding neighbourhoods to take longer routes to reach cremation grounds. Residents who could earlier reach the B.B. Road crematorium after travelling about half a kilometre now had to travel nearly eight km, he said.

Following the rains from Cyclone Murasu, repair work is underway to fix potholes formed on the road at Ponniamman Koil Street near Manjambakkam under Manali Zone by the Greater Chennai Corporation on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

Mr. Kumarasamy alleged that road works awarded during the previous regime had been stopped after the change of government, with officials citing a lack of funds. He said estimates and repair works had not been prepared in advance of the monsoon. He also criticised the absence of advance arrangements such as deploying tractors, generators and pumps in vulnerable locations.

K. Shanmugam, president of the Federation of North Chennai Resident Welfare Associations, said the rain had not caused major flooding in his area. However, water collected in depressions along the road from Chinnamadam to Thiruthangal Nadar College because of its uneven surface. He also flagged K.K. Salai in Manali, a key link road stretching about two–three km towards Manali market, where sections had been dug up for stormwater drain works but had not been properly restored.
Greater Chennai corporation attening to potholes in Kumaran Nagar in Madhavaram on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

S. Vishanth of the Ennore Solidarity Group said water had stagnated in parts of Athipattu near Ennore, but the situation had subsequently improved. He said the area where he was located was relatively elevated and had experienced less water accumulation.

articles.title: What is ‘Guidance’, Tamil Nadu’s nodal agency for investments? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The story so far: Guidance, the nodal agency of the Tamil Nadu government for investment promotion and single-window facilitation, is in the limelight for the wrong reasons. Former Chief Ministers M.K. Stalin and Edappadi K. Palaniswami have accused the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government of having “immobilised” the body.

Guidance, earlier known as the Tamil Nadu Guidance and Export Promotion Bureau, was established as a non-profit registered society on July 15, 1992, with the objective of attracting investment proposals into Tamil Nadu. It is mandated to span the full spectrum of investment promotion activities, with a focus on generating leads, facilitating projects, and providing post-investment support. The body is expected to catch the emerging market trends and formulate new sectoral policies, strengthen industry-academia collaboration, and engage with trade bodies and multilateral agencies. It hopes to play a crucial role in making the State a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036, a goal of the present government.

articles.title: Petronet LNG reports 52.3% growth in net profits, in talks for availing undelivered cargoes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia.
The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share.
The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year.
Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore.
The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year.
Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year.
Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year.

Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure.
“On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said.
The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end.
Mr. Singh told reporters that the contractual terms have provisions to recoup the lost cargoes for one year after the expiry of the current contract period, that is, May 2028.
He stated that Petronet LNG lost an average 9-10 cargoes each month in the last eight months, thus, about 75-80 cargoes whilst it has received 6 cargoes from the supplier.
